messages:
sam_customer: Hi team — after tightening our egress allowlist and enabling corporate TLS inspection, our websocket streams to our Private Redwood endpoint intermittently stall. Connection stays ESTABLISHED, no 5xx, then client stops receiving chunks for ~90-140s and finally resumes. This only affects streaming endpoints (chat/stream), normal REST calls are fine. Can share pcapng.

alex_support: thanks — is this only ws-based streaming or also http/1.1 chunked responses? any client lib details (node/go/browser)?

sam_customer: just websockets (upgraded TLS). We have both Node (server-side) and some browser clients. Node service writes small update frames ~50-200B every 100-200ms. Browser clients show same stall. We started seeing this right after the FW change yesterday.

maria_oncall: tagging eng-sre & networks. @chris_sre @jordan_networks any instincts? Middlebox idle/inspection seems likely.

chris_sre: yep, classic DPI/middlebox behavior. Many inspection proxies buffer small TLS records until either a byte threshold or idle timer. If the app produces lots of small TLS records, the proxy may hold them and then flush on timer — gives the exact stall you're describing. Do you have a packet capture showing TLS record sizes and inter-packet gaps?

sam_customer: attached a short pcapng: I see repeated TLS application data records ~200B every 150ms, then silence for ~120s, then a burst of many records. FW team says they have a 2-minute idle TCP timeout and TLS inspection enabled.

jordan_networks: that matches. DPI often reconstructs flows and waits for larger application payloads before forwarding to reduce context switching. If they can't disable inspection, the options are to change client behavior (coalesce writes, increase keepalives) or bypass the DPI for these flows.

fw_ops: we can't disable inspection globally, but we can add bypass rules for specific SNI/hostname or destination IPs. We'll need the exact hostnames and, if possible, cert details (serial/thumbprint) to safely bypass only the Redwood endpoint.

alex_support: recommended steps (short list):
- enable app-level websocket keepalive (ping/application keepalive) every 20-30s
- shorten TCP keepalive so it hits before FW idle timeout
- request DPI bypass for your Private endpoint by SNI/hostname + port 443
- as a debugging step, run a synthetic openssl/ngrep test to verify midstream buffering

chris_sre: example sysctl (linux):
```
# apply as root
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=30
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_intvl=10
sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_probes=3
```
App ping example (Node):
```
const ws = new WebSocket(url);
setInterval(() => {
  if (ws.readyState === WebSocket.OPEN) ws.send(JSON.stringify({_type:'rw_keepalive'}));
}, 25000);
```
Note: browsers don't expose ws.ping; use an app-level JSON keepalive or a tiny binary frame.

chris_sre: debugging shell snippet (from inside network):
```
# use openssl s_client to open TLS then type small payloads manually
openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.example.com:443 -servername private.redwood.example.com
# paste upgrade headers then send small payloads at 1s intervals, watch captures
```
If you see the same hold/release pattern there, it's the middlebox.

sam_customer: FW team asked for cert details and SNI info. alex, can you provide exact recommended hostnames and a note about certificate pin info we can hand to fw_ops? They don't want to bypass on IP only.

alex_support: provide these to fw_ops:
- hostname: use the exact Private endpoint hostname from your console (private.redwood.example.com in this thread as placeholder)
- SNI: same as hostname (SNI-based bypass preferred)
- certificate: you can fetch CN/SAN and serial from the console > TLS settings. If they require a thumbprint, export the cert and compute SHA256. We'll DM an abbreviated IP range for your region for a fallback, but SNI bypass is ideal since our infra uses dynamic IPs.

fw_ops: ok we can add an SNI bypass rule for that hostname + port 443. we'll apply only for the service account IP blocks you provided. ETA 90m.

jordan_networks: additional note — some TLS stacks (old OpenSSL, default Go behavior) produce many small TLS records; others coalesce. If bypass isn't possible, another mitigation is to tune the application to coalesce writes into larger TLS records or to enable TLS record size tuning where supported. Also increasing the frequency of application-level pings tends to keep the DPI from idling out.

sam_customer: doing keepalive ping + sysctl change on our container hosts now. We'll also ask fw_ops to apply SNI bypass. We'll run a 1-hour smoke test after changes and share a pcap if issues persist.

alex_support: thanks — if bypass fixes it, great. If not, please share the pcapng with UTC timestamps and a short repro script (small curl/openssl or small Node script that sends periodic frames). We'll correlate with our ingress logs and escalate to infra.

sam_customer: update: fw_ops applied SNI bypass and we enabled app-level keepalive (25s). Initial 30m smoke looks stable, no midstream stalls. Looks like a combination of DPI buffering + firewall idle timer. Thanks everyone :tada:

maria_oncall: excellent. leaving ticket open for 24h to monitor, then we'll close and add KB guidance to Private deployment docs about egress allowlists, DPI, and websocket keepalives.

deploy-bot: Incident follow-up created: INS-2026-0919 (add WebSocket keepalive / TCP keepalive guidance to Private docs)
